concepts.name: Quantum Information Processing

concepts.name: Weyl Scalar
concepts.contribution: The Weyl scalar is a quantity that describes the curvature of spacetime. It is defined as the trace of the Ricci tensor and is an important invariant in differential geometry and general relativity.

concepts.name: Tetrad

concepts.name: Spin Connection

concepts.name: Herglotz Lagrangian
concepts.contribution: The Herglotz Lagrangian is an action functional that incorporates a scaling symmetry of degree one, which is constructed from a scalar field Φ and its conjugate f.

concepts.name: Scaling Symmetry
concepts.contribution: A scaling symmetry of degree one is a transformation that preserves the form of an action functional, while also preserving the physical properties of the system being described.

concepts.name: PQCD

concepts.name: Strange Quark Condensate

concepts.name: Purcell enhancement of single-photon emitters

2605.05785v1.title: Optical Pulling Force in Carbon Nanotubes: Manifestation of Nonlocal Conductivity

concepts.name: Optical Force in Carbon Nanotubes
concepts.contribution: This paper introduces a theory for the optical force acting on carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with nonlocal conductivity, taking into account edge effects due to finite length.

concepts.name: Nonlocal Conductivity
concepts.contribution: The theory considers spatial dispersion, a nonlocal effect that arises from the finite size of CNTs and leads to a non-conservative force.

concepts.name: Spatial Dispersion
concepts.contribution: This paper explores the impact of spatial dispersion on the optical force in CNTs, showing its significance for understanding the behavior of these nanostructures.

concepts.name: Carbon Nanotubes
concepts.contribution: The work focuses on achiral CNTs in vacuum, but future generalizations can be made to more complex structures, such as suspended CNTs or CNTs in different environments.

2605.05783v1.title: Isomer depletion via nuclear excitation by inelastic electron scattering

concepts.name: Isomer Depletion via NEIES
concepts.contribution: This paper explores the process of isomer depletion via Nuclear Electric Excitation and Scattering (NEIES), which involves the excitation of a nucleus at an isomeric state through NEIES and subsequent decay to the ground state. The authors investigate the NEIES cross sections for various isotopes and their effects on isomer depletion. This work has significant implications for energy storage materials, as it provides insight into the mechanisms underlying the depleting of nuclear isomers.

concepts.name: Nuclear Electric Excitation and Scattering (NEIES)
concepts.contribution: This paper introduces Nuclear Electric Excitation and Scattering (NEIES) as a process that excites a nucleus through the interaction with an incoming electron. The authors discuss the selection rules, angular momentum quantum numbers, and energy dependence of NEIES cross sections for various nuclear transitions.

concepts.name: Energy Storage Materials
concepts.contribution: This research contributes to the understanding of energy storage materials by investigating the isomer depletion via NEIES. The study of isomer deple- tion mechanisms provides valuable insights into the long-term stability and performance of these materials, which are crucial for various applications in fields such as medicine, industry, and nuclear energy.

concepts.name: Isomeric States
concepts.contribution: This paper focuses on the study of isomeric states, specifically their decay modes and mechanisms. The authors explore the role of NEIES in the depleting of nuclear isomers and its implications for energy storage materials. Understanding the behavior of isomeric states is essential for optimizing the performance and longevity of these materials.

2605.05764v1.title: Weighted Phase-Space Paths for Exact Wigner Dynamics

concepts.name: Wigner Function
concepts.contribution: The Wigner function is a mathematical representation of the quantum state, which is used to describe the quantum system in phase space. This paper explores the properties and applications of the Wigner function, particularly in the context of exact dynamics and dynamical nonclassicality.

concepts.name: Moyal Residual
concepts.contribution: The Moyal residual is a correction term that arises in the evolution of the Wigner function, which represents the difference between the exact dynamics and the Fokker-Planck closure. This paper studies the properties and importance of the Moyal residual in understanding dynamical nonclassicality.

concepts.name: Signed Path Representation
concepts.contribution: The signed path representation is a new formulation of the Wigner function, which takes into account the sign of the contributions to the Wigner function. This paper explores the properties and applications of this representation, particularly in understanding dynamical nonclassicality.

concepts.name: Fluctuation Relations
concepts.contribution: This paper introduces a new type of fluctuation relation that compares forward and reversed weighted path contributions, rather than just positive probabilities. This relation provides insights into the nature of quantum dynamics and can be used to diagnose dynamical nonclassicality.

2605.05721v1.title: Electronic and Photonic Integration of Single Quantum Emitters in 2D Materials

concepts.name: Vertical Graphene/hBN/WSe2 Tunnel-Junction LED
concepts.contribution: Demonstrates the fabrication and operation of an atomically thin quantum light-emitting diode (QLED) based on a vertical graphene/hBN/WSe2 heterostructure, showing electrical excitation of monolayer WSe2 with localized emission near threshold.

concepts.name: Lateral Split-Gate p-i-n Junction
concepts.contribution: Introduces an electrostatically defined junction for confining electron-hole overlap to a designed intrinsic in-plane recombination zone, enabling deterministic and electrically driven single-photon emission from localized defects in monolayer TMDs.

concepts.name: Double-Barrier Vertical Graphene/hBN/WSe2 LED
concepts.contribution: Explores the effect of thin hBN tunnel barriers on carrier injection and defect emission in a vertical graphene/hBN/WSe2 heterostructure, demonstrating the potential for narrowband, antibunched emission from localized defects.

2605.05663v1.title: Scalar-Field Reconstruction of Ricci--Gauss--Bonnet Dark Energy in Hořava--Lifshitz Cosmology

concepts.name: Holographic Principle
concepts.contribution: The holographic principle is a theoretical framework in physics that proposes that the information contained in a region of spacetime can be encoded on its surface. This paper applies the holographic principle to the study of dark energy and its relation to Hoêva-Lifshitz gravity.

concepts.name: Hoêva-Lifshitz Gravity
concepts.contribution: Hoêva-Lifshitz gravity is a theoretical framework that describes the behavior of gravity at high energies and densities. This paper uses Hoêva-Lifshitz gravity to model dark energy and its relation to the universe's evolution.

concepts.name: Dark Energy
concepts.contribution: Dark energy is a hypothetical form of energy that is thought to be responsible for the accelerating expansion of the universe. This paper studies the properties of dark energy in the context of Hoêva-Lifshitz gravity and its relation to the holographic principle.

concepts.name: Ricci-Gauss-Bonnet Theories
concepts.contribution: The Ricci-Gauss-Bonnet theories are a class of gravitational theories that describe the behavior of spacetime in terms of curvature and topology. This paper applies these theories to study dark energy and its relation to Hoêva-Lifshitz gravity.

2605.05658v1.title: Quantum-classical solvation hydrodynamics: Hamiltonian functionals and dissipation

concepts.name: Hamiltonian Mechanics
concepts.contribution: This paper establishes a Hamiltonian framework for modeling mixed quantum-classical hydrodynamics, providing a unified approach to understanding the dynamics of fluid flows and scalar function transport.

concepts.name: Poisson Brackets
concepts.contribution: The authors develop a systematic method for adding transported functions to Hamiltonian hydrodynamic systems, utilizing the Poisson bracket structure to capture the necessary equations of motion.

concepts.name: Hydrodynamic Closure
concepts.contribution: This paper presents a novel approach to closing the mixed quantum-classical Koopman model within a Hamiltonian framework, providing a consistent and rigorous methodology for modeling complex fluid flows and scalar function transport.

concepts.name: Lie-Poisson Systems
concepts.contribution: The authors demonstrate that the extended Poisson bracket structure introduced in this paper satisfies the defining properties of Lie-Poisson systems, ensuring the validity and consistency of the resulting equations of motion.

2605.05635v1.title: Adaptive ray tracing and photon ring signatures of rotating dark-matter-dressed black holes

concepts.name: Black Hole Physics
concepts.contribution: This paper explores the effects of dark matter on rotating black hole spacetimes, providing new insights into their behavior and appearance.

concepts.name: General Relativity
concepts.contribution: The paper uses general relativity to describe the metric and other fundamental aspects of rotating black hole spacetimes in the presence of dark matter.

concepts.name: Numerical Methods
concepts.contribution: The authors employ numerical methods to simulate the behavior of photons emitted by a observer screen placed near a rotating black hole, allowing them to study the effects of dark matter on the observed image.

2605.05634v1.title: Relativistic mean-field study of the neutron star inner crust using the asymmetric finite difference method

concepts.name: Effective Nucleon Mass
concepts.contribution: An increase in effective nucleon mass tends to diminish the nucleon density in the central region, producing an effect comparable to that of increasing the symmetry energy slope L while maintaining the effective mass.

concepts.name: Symmetry Energy Slope
concepts.contribution: The parameter set with a larger symmetry energy slope generally exhibits a higher neutron density at the surface, whereas a smaller slope yields a higher central density.

concepts.name: Inner Crust Environment
concepts.contribution: Extremely neutron-rich nuclei like 950Sn exhibit complex nucleon density distributions that arise from quantum shell effects and the interplay between different nuclear forces.

2605.05633v1.title: Eigenstate-Selective Entangled Two-Photon Absorption in Monolayer WSe$_2$

concepts.name: Pumping Rate Modulation
concepts.contribution: This paper introduces a novel method for tuning the pumping rate of cross-circular biphoton states, which is controlled by the Bell phase and results in a zero excitation to dark eigenstates at φ = π.

concepts.name: Exchange Symmetry
concepts.contribution: The model exploits the exchange symmetry within the configuration basis to enforce a zero excitation to dark eigenstates at φ = π, which is a novel feature of this paper.

concepts.name: Spectral Detuning
concepts.contribution: This paper shows that spectral detuning can be used to suppress excitation to bright eigenstates, and that the combination of spectral detuning and exchange symmetry results in a suppression of excitation to dark eigenstates at φ = π.

concepts.name: Geometric Coupling Efficiency
concepts.contribution: The paper introduces geometric coupling efficiencies as a measure of how strongly each eigenstate couples to the cross-circular sector, which are used to quantify the pumping rate modulation.

2605.05631v1.title: Wandering Exponents and the Free Energy of the High-Dimensional Elastic Polymer

concepts.name: Wandering Exponent
concepts.contribution: The wandering exponent is a measure of how fast a polymer chain moves in space and time, and it has implications for our understanding of transport phenomena in disordered systems.

concepts.name: Diffusivity
concepts.contribution: A model is considered diffusive if its wandering exponent is 1/2, meaning that the chain moves at a moderate pace. This is in contrast to superdiffusive models, which exhibit faster-than-average motion.

concepts.name: Superdiffusivity
concepts.contribution: In superdiffusive models, the wandering exponent exceeds 1/2, indicating that the polymer chain moves more quickly than average. This can lead to enhanced transport properties and unique behaviors.

concepts.name: Quenched Free Energy
concepts.contribution: The quenched free energy is a measure of the average energy of a system with randomly distributed parameters. In this paper, we use the Parisi functional to compute the asymptotic free energy of a polymer chain model.

2605.05625v1.title: Quantum Kernels for Parity-Structured Classification: A Hybrid Pipeline

concepts.name: Quantum Machine Learning
concepts.contribution: This paper proposes a quantum machine learning approach that leverages the exponential capacity of quantum circuits to capture complex combinatorial structures, outperforming classical baseline methods on parity-structured classification tasks.

concepts.name: Parity Complexity
concepts.contribution: The paper reveals a phase transition around n=9, where binary encoding alone suffices for low-n values, but the quantum ZZ kernel provides a growing advantage as n increases, highlighting the importance of representation design in quantum machine learning.

concepts.name: Kernel Methods
concepts.contribution: This work demonstrates that quantum machine learning models are indeed kernel methods, leveraging the feature Hilbert space to capture complex relationships between data points and outperforming classical baseline methods on supervised learning tasks.

concepts.name: Quantum Advantage
concepts.contribution: The paper does not claim a general 'quantum advantage' in complexity-theoretic terms but rather highlights the importance of representation design in quantum machine learning, demonstrating a proof-of-concept on synthetic data and paving the way for future research.

2605.05624v1.title: The General Structure of Trilinear Equations

concepts.name: Tomimatsu-Sato Spacetime
concepts.contribution: The Tomimatsu-Sato spacetime is a type of axially symmetric black hole solution in general relativity, first introduced by Akio Tomimatsu and Hiroshi Sato in 1972. This paper provides an example of the YTSF integrable structure in the context of Tomimatsu-Sato geometry.

concepts.name: YTSF Integrable Structure
concepts.contribution: The YTSF (Yang-Tau-Soliton Functional) integrable structure is a mathematical framework for studying nonlinear evolution equations. This paper demonstrates its application to the stationary axisymmetric Einstein field equations, providing an example of its realization in Tomimatsu-Sato geometry.

concepts.name: Soliton Equations
concepts.contribution: Soliton equations are a type of nonlinear partial differential equation that describe the propagation of solitons, stable waves with finite energy. This paper uses soliton theory as a background to study the YTSF integrable structure in the context of Tomimatsu-Sato geometry.

concepts.name: Gravitational Field Equations
concepts.contribution: The gravitational field equations are a set of nonlinear partial differential equations that describe the motion of mass and energy in curved spacetime. This paper uses the YTSF integrable structure to study the solutions to these equations, specifically in the context of Tomimatsu-Sato geometry.

2605.05617v1.title: Static-Field Tunneling Ionization in Space-Fractional Quantum Mechanics

concepts.name: Tunneling Ionization
concepts.contribution: The paper presents a new tunneling ionization model that incorporates the nonlocal nature of the kinetic energy, leading to a more accurate description of strong-field physics.

concepts.name: Fractional Power-Law Dispersion
concepts.contribution: The model introduces a parameter α that governs the dispersion relation, allowing for a smooth transition from classical to quantum behavior and providing a new framework for understanding nonlocal transport effects.

concepts.name: Nonlocal Kinetic Energy
concepts.contribution: The paper explores the implications of nonlocal kinetic energy on tunneling ionization, highlighting its importance in understanding the complex dynamics involved in strong-field physics.

concepts.name: Strong-Field Physics
concepts.contribution: The model is embedded within the broader framework of strong-field physics, ensuring continuity with established theories and providing a foundation for further research on continuum dynamics and recollision-based phenomena.

2605.05608v1.title: Dynamical Signatures of Floquet Topology in Wave Packet Dynamics

concepts.name: Floquet Topology
concepts.contribution: A theoretical framework for understanding the topological properties of periodic systems under time-dependent perturbations.

concepts.name: Zak Phase
concepts.contribution: A quantification of the topological charge of a system, related to its Floquet Hamiltonian and used as a bulk invariant.

concepts.name: Band Inversion
concepts.contribution: A transition in a periodic system's band structure, resulting from changes in the Floquet Hamiltonian and leading to distinct dynamical behavior.

concepts.name: Time-Dependent Quantum Systems
concepts.contribution: Systems where the Hamiltonian or other parameters change with time, requiring a description of their evolution over parameter space.

2605.05605v1.title: Mixed Global Dynamics of the Forced Vibro-Impact Oscillator with Coulomb Friction and its Symplectic Structure, KAM Tori, and Persistence

concepts.name: Filippov differential inclusion
concepts.contribution: Provides a rigorous framework for modeling the forced vibro-impact oscillator, including the Filippov set-valued vector field F and its associated inequalities.

concepts.name: Lift construction
concepts.contribution: Establishes the conjugacy between the lifted flow and the original Filippov flow, restricted to non-sticking trajectories, through a universal-cover construction.

concepts.name: KAM theorem for elliptic non-sticking periodic orbits
concepts.contribution: Proves the existence of invariant smooth closed curves around any elliptic non-resonant non-degenerate non-sticking T-periodic orbit using the KAM theorem, with measure complement O(δ5/2).

concepts.name: Saddle-center bifurcation
concepts.contribution: Characterizes the parameter-dependent saddle-center value and establishes a non-degenerate bifurcation at f = 4(2F + Rω2 - Fπ)/π2, with explicit local normal form derived by the Morse lemma.

2605.05604v1.title: Temporal Coarse-Graining as the Origin of Macroscopic Friction in Quantum Spin Chains via Data-Driven Liouvillian Extraction

concepts.name: Liouvillian
concepts.contribution: A mathematical framework for describing the evolution of quantum systems.

concepts.name: Temporal Coarse-Graining
concepts.contribution: The process of averaging out high-frequency fluctuations to reveal macroscopic behavior.

concepts.name: Einstein Relation
concepts.contribution: A fundamental connection between transport coefficients and the diffusion coefficient in materials.

2605.05589v1.title: Galois Solvability of Finite-Size Bethe Solutions in the Heisenberg Chain

concepts.name: Bethe Ansatz
concepts.contribution: A mathematical approach used to solve exactly solvable quantum many-body systems, including the Heisenberg chain. This paper extends the known symbolic ground states of the Heisenberg chain to up to the ten-site case, revealing that finite-size Bethe solutions can rapidly develop unsolvable algebraic complexity despite the integrability of the underlying model.

concepts.name: Galois Groups
concepts.contribution: A mathematical concept used to determine the solvability of polynomial equations. In this paper, it is used to analyze the irreducible polynomials that govern the Bethe roots and their unsolvability for chains of eight or more sites.

concepts.name: Heisenberg Chain
concepts.contribution: A one-dimensional quantum many-body system with antiferromagnetic interactions. This paper presents explicit symbolic ground states for this model up to the ten-site case, providing insight into the behavior of finite-size Bethe solutions and their limitations.

concepts.name: Quantum Integrability
concepts.contribution: A property of quantum many-body systems that allows them to be exactly solved. This paper explores the relationship between integrability and exact solvability, demonstrating that these concepts are distinct despite the integrability of certain models.

2605.05565v1.title: Squeezed spectra and back-to-back correlations of protons and antiprotons at RHIC energies

concepts.name: Squeezing effect in heavy-ion collisions
concepts.contribution: The squeezing effect is a phenomenon observed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions where particle interactions within the medium induce an in-medium mass modification, leading to squeezed back-to-back correlations of particle-antiparticle pairs.

concepts.name: In-medium mass modification
concepts.contribution: An in-medium mass modification refers to a change in the mass of particles within the hot and dense matter created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, which can lead to various effects such as squeezing back-to-back correlations and changes in single-particle invariant momentum distributions.

concepts.name: Back-to-back correlation
concepts.contribution: A back-to-back correlation refers to a phenomenon where two particles are found in the opposite direction of each other, often observed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The squeezing effect can lead to an increase in back-to-back correlations due to in-medium mass modifications.

concepts.name: Heavy-ion collision experiments
concepts.contribution: Heavy-ion collision experiments aim to study the properties of the quark-gluon plasma created in these collisions, including the effects of in-medium mass modifications and squeezing back-to-back correlations. The RHIC (Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider) at Brookhaven National Laboratory is one such experiment.

concepts.name: Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background
concepts.contribution: This paper explores the detection and analysis of stochastic gravitational wave background signals from eccentric stellar black hole binaries in the LISA band.

concepts.name: Eccentric Stellar Black Hole Binaries
concepts.contribution: The study focuses on the characteristics of eccentric sBBHs, including their initial orbital frequencies, eccentricities, and thermal distributions.

concepts.name: LISA Sensitivity and Detection Thresholds
concepts.contribution: This paper evaluates the sensitivity of LISA to detect stochastic signals from eccentric sBBHs and assesses the impact of Galactic foreground noise on signal detection.

concepts.name: Bayesian Inference and Model Parameters
concepts.contribution: The authors perform a comprehensive Bayesian analysis to estimate the initial eccentricity, orbital frequency, and other model parameters of detected sBBHs.
